Published online:
September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
Fed Governor Waller signals he would support holding rates steady at the September 15-16 meeting if August inflation data shows continued cooling, but explicitly keeps a rate hike on the table if inflation surprises to the upside. Current fed funds rate sits at 3.50%-3.75%, described as only mildly restrictive. Waller downplays tariffs and energy as persistent inflation drivers but flags upside risks from AI-driven tech goods prices, energy price levels, and potential further tariff increases. Post-remarks, market odds of a September hike fell to just above 50% from ~60%.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 60 (meaningful — a hike is explicitly on the table and was the prior market base case)
Probability of increase: ~50% (markets revised down from ~60% post-remarks)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 70 (Waller's stated inclination, conditional on soft inflation print)
Probability of holding: ~50% (mirror of hike odds post-remarks)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (cuts are entirely absent from the discussion)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -15 (Slightly dovish lean vs. prior expectations — Waller's remarks shifted market pricing away from a near-certain hike toward a coin-flip, but the explicit hike threat, upside inflation risks flagged, and the broader hawkish Fed communication backdrop prevent a strongly dovish read)
